name: Memory map fix for PCs with memory above 4 GB
description: Windows 98 stops reading the firmware's memory map (INT 15h E820) at the first range above 4 GiB, so on PCs with more than about 3 GB of RAM it can miss reserved areas listed after it and use device memory as RAM: random crashes and resource conflicts. SweetLow's fix (via patcher9x by JHRobotics, MIT) lets it skip such ranges and read on. Applied only where the hardware scan finds memory above 4 GiB; older PCs don't need it.

ops.name: VMM
ops.comment: Windows loads SYSTEM\VMM32\VMM.VXD in place of the copy packed in VMM32.VXD (the cpu-speed-fix module may have extracted it already).
W98 >4G resource patch (patcher9x g4resfix, after SweetLow's VMM_4GRes_Fix): 3 jump offsets, so the E820 loop skips a range above 4 GiB instead of ending.
